rule: good. both sides are bare kinds, so this becomes the kind-to-kind relation rather than a per-instance rule, and lantern_station gets its head genus with the noun modifier correctly left unexposed.
texts: mixed: the rule fires and a fresh heir is minted for each retirement, but "the lantern-station" collapses into one single shared station, so the parse says every heir of every retiring Keeper inherits the same one station. Name whose station it is so it varies with the Keeper: "When a senior Keeper retires, an heir inherits that Keeper's lantern-station."

good. the rule fires, and here both the heir and the station vary per Keeper — unlike the retirement variant, where the station collapsed to one shared constant — with the dying Keeper correctly the undergoer and no tense on the generic.

bad: "an" plus an ordinary verb makes this one particular station and one particular family rather than the standing rule you mean, so nothing generalises to inherited stations at large; "in the family" is also recorded as physical containment, as though the station sat inside a family. Rewrite the subject as a bare plural: "Inherited stations stay in the family." If the point is ownership rather than place, say so with a possession verb, e.g. "A Keeper's family keeps that Keeper's inherited station."

good. the obligation becomes a firing rule over every station transfer with the Council as approver, approve takes the evaluating-object role, station_transfer is decomposed to its head genus, and "any" is kept as a recorded quantifier word.
